data.body:
FINAL ROOT CAUSE for the patchset-2 failure, recorded because it is subtle and the ticket would otherwise imply the first diagnosis was the whole story.

The py3.12 failure was test_git_probe_timeout_ignores_a_test_monkeypatch_of_time_sleep --
'DID NOT RAISE TimeoutExpired'. Mechanism, proven rather than assumed:

The probe SIGKILLs a stalled shim, and patchset 1 introduced RE-SAMPLING afterwards. So for the first
time a LATER shim invocation reads a counter file an EARLIER one was killed while writing.
Path.write_text truncates before it writes, so a kill inside that window leaves the counter EMPTY.
The next shim then dies on int(''), check=True turns that into CalledProcessError, and head() /
porcelain() catch SubprocessError and return None -- which means 'not a git repo' for a repo that
plainly is one. So pytest.raises(TimeoutExpired) saw no exception.

IMPORTANT SCOPE NOTE: this is a defect in the guard's TEST SHIM, not in the shipped probe. The
shipped probe's state is the git repo, which it only reads.

Fix: the shim writes its counter atomically (temp file + os.replace), so the authoritative file is
never truncated and no kill can leave it empty. The counter READ stays strict -- tolerating a corrupt
counter would have masked this bug class rather than removed it. That is the right call and worth
preserving against a future 'just make it tolerant' edit.

My three follow-up questions were answered rather than deflected: observed_outer_timeouts[0] >= 30
was NOT the failure (the original reasoning held); no other _blocking_git caller relied on the old
single-mode behaviour; and bug 9a17 has NOT recurred (zero matches for 'crashed' / 'test_editor_e2e'
/ 'node down' in the failing log).

MAIN-GREEN EVIDENCE, with a corroborating detail: sweep (macos, full suite) on main at 1af45065465e
  before (6b034b9f8224): 19243 passed, 72 skipped, 422 warnings, 1 ERROR in 2687.89s
  after  (1af45065465e): 19268 passed, 72 skipped,  66 warnings,  0 errors in 1735.79s
The 422 -> 66 drop in [rebar-ci-timing] warnings independently corroborates the diagnosis: the
original failure was on an unusually contended runner, which is precisely why a single 5s sample was
not a safe estimator of a probe's latency.

Guard self-tests were run 23 passed x5 consecutive AND x3 under load average 6-9 -- i.e. the fix was
exercised under the contention that caused the bug, not just on an idle machine.

On the close discrepancy the implementer flagged: the 12:58 close was MINE, through the completion
gate. Correctly raised rather than silently accepted.
